To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the patients with breast cancer have a significantly reduced cellular immune competence as compared to normal subjects and the impairment in the cellular immunity was directly proportional to the clinical stage and prognosis of the disease.
the immune system of patients with breast cancer was impaired in its ability to produce delayed hypersensitivity response and to produce T-lymphocyte and E-rosetre.
the patients with breast cancer have impaired immune response to primary and secondary antigens and that there was a good correlation of this impairment with tumour load.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of immune competence in patients of breast cancer by multiparametric observation and its correlation with clinical parameters.
the development of an effective, non-invasive, and inexpensive technique to measure the level of the immune response in the breast.
the study of the immune status in breast cancer patients and its correlation with prognosis.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the immune system in breast cancer patients is impaired in all its parameters, and the impairment of immune status is directly related to tumour load, prognosis of the patients, and tumour recurrence.
there is an impaired cell mediated immunity in breast cancer patients and the extent of impairment correlates with the clinical stage of the disease.
the immune status of breast cancer patients is impaired and is related to the prognosis of the patients.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the cellular immunity in patients of breast cancer was impaired and correlated with clinical stage of the disease and prognosis.
there are significant differences between breast cancer and normal controls in the cellular immunity and immunoglobulin levels.
a significant impairment in cellular immune status was observed in the patients with breast cancer.
The main takeaway from our work is that
there are several different types of breast cancer, and that each of those types is associated with different risk factors.
we can identify patients who are more likely to respond to immune therapy based on their T cells and their ability to make cytokines.
there are several factors that influence a patient's response to cancer treatment.
